summary: Proxy normalizes OIDC client_id to lowercase, breaking app_role->role bindings for service accounts in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer QuantaHealth reports intermittent 403s for scheduled service-account calls to the admin API after migrating their private VPC ingress to the 2026-02 ingress-config bundle. Interactive UI logins are unaffected.

Impact:
- Service workers using client_credentials flow receive 403 on admin API calls which require service-role bindings.
- Affects production jobs that run hourly (billing reconciles, export workers).
- Customer reports ~30% job failures across critical pipelines since 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC.

Environment:
- Customer private deployment (VPC) in eu-west region, running Redwood Private 1.8.2 with vendor ingress (nginx-based) using our managed ingress-config bundle 2026-02.
- Identity provider: Azure AD (v2) using appRoles mapped via resource_access -> <client-id> -> roles.
- Affected endpoints: /admin/v1/tenants/* (admin-api).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Create Azure AD application with an appRole assigned to the service principal.
2) Obtain token via client_credentials (scope: api://<client-id>/.default). Token payload contains resource_access with the client-id in original case (e.g., 6F3A2B10-ABcd-4f11-9F0a-3e2aB1cD7eE).
3) Request POST /admin/v1/tenants/123/actions with Authorization: Bearer <token>.
4) Observe 403 and response body: {"error":"rbac: no matching role binding for principal"}.

Observed behavior:
- Token introspection shows claims include resource_access keyed by the cased client-id as issued by Azure AD.
- Edge/ingress access logs show header X-Client-Id present but lowercased (6f3a2b10-abcd-4f11-9f0a-3e2ab1cd7ee).
- Identity service lookup for role bindings uses original client-id key (case-sensitive map) and fails to find the binding, resulting in a deny.
- Interactive flows (OIDC code flow) map to group claims and are not impacted.

Expected behavior:
- Client credentials tokens should permit service principals bound to roles regardless of header case normalization performed by ingress. Identity service should handle client-id canonicalization or ingress should preserve case.

Logs & traces (redacted):
- Admin API trace: trace_id=tr-e4b2f3a, response=403, rbac_lookup_key=6F3A2B10-ABcd-4f11-9F0a-3e2aB1cD7eE, x-client-id-header=6f3a2b10-abcd-4f11-9f0a-3e2ab1cd7ee
- Ingress debug (2026-03-09T02:07:12Z): rewrite map applied to X-Client-Id header -> tolower().
- Token dump (customer provided, redacted): {"aud":"api://6F3A2B10-ABcd-4f11-9F0a-3e2aB1cD7eE", "resource_access": {"6F3A2B10-ABcd-4f11-9F0a-3e2aB1cD7eE": {"roles": ["service_admin"]}}}

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced in our staging when enabling the 2026-02 ingress-config bundle with header normalization enabled; disabling the header normalization step restores expected behavior.
- The ingress config change introduced a generic header canonicalization map to reduce header key duplication for multi-tenant hostnames; it inadvertently applied to custom headers (X-Client-Id).
- Identity lookup code uses the exact map key from token resource_access; there is no case-insensitive fallback.
- Hypothesis: two mitigation approaches - (A) stop ingress from lowercasing X-Client-Id, or (B) make identity service perform case-insensitive matching for client-id keys (normalize both token keys and internal role lookup keys to the same case).

Customer impact & priority:
- P1 / Sev1: production jobs failing with business impact. Customer has asked for short-term workaround and a code/config fix plan.

Temporary workaround provided to customer (2026-03-10):
- We advised customer to apply an ingress patch to re-enable header case preservation (preserve_client_id_case: true) which they applied to their environment; their job failures dropped to 0-2% immediately.
- Recommended a scheduled restart of ingress sidecars during maintenance window to ensure patch is active.

Proposed long-term fix & plan:
1) Roll back header canonicalization for custom headers in ingress-config (engineering change). Target: hotfix release 2026-03-18. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood/ingress-config/pull/598.
2) Add identity-service tolerant lookup: normalize client-id keys in token introspection to uppercase before lookup or perform case-insensitive match. This will be backward-compatible. Target: identity-service PR 2026-03-22.
3) Add a conformance test to private deployment upgrade path to ensure header policies do not alter custom id headers.

Next steps assigned:
- Ravi (assignee) to coordinate ingress-config PR and private customer rollout (owner).
- Eng (identity) to scope minor change for case-insensitive lookup and provide ETA.
- SRE/Support to schedule targeted rollout for QuantaHealth with rollback plan.

Notes:
- This is likely to affect any private customers who rely on case-sensitive client-id keys in resource_access tokens and who accept our managed ingress-config bundle.
- Add to release notes: "Ingress header canonicalization disabled for X-Client-Id by default" and migration notes for customers who opted into the 2026-02 bundle.
